clue.text: Hypocrisy of twins given flag to hold

indicators.note: the twins are given the flag to hold, so one word sits inside the other

parts.note: a pair of identical things are doubles
a standard is a flag or banner

explanation.surface: Someone accuses a pair of twins of hypocrisy for being handed a flag to carry.
explanation.definitionFit: Applying different rules to oneself and others is the essence of hypocrisy.

clue.text: A cut in sugar drink is of great interest

parts.note: sugar is an endearment, like dear

indicators.note: the cut goes in, splitting the drink between its second and third letters

parts.note: a tot is a small drink of spirits
a means one
to shear is to cut

explanation.surface: Someone finds a sugary drink with a slice in it fascinating.
explanation.walkthrough: The cut-in phrase lands between the second and third letters of the drink, so TO is left before it and the final T after it.
explanation.definitionFit: Something held dear to one's heart is cherished, hence a matter of great interest or concern.

clue.text: A Parisian channel is not reliable

parts.note: un is French for a, as a Parisian would say it
a sound is a sea channel or strait

explanation.surface: A French waterway is untrustworthy for navigation.
explanation.definitionFit: Unsound reasoning or structures are faulty and so cannot be trusted.

clue.text: Place to get approval? In your dreams!

definitions.meaning: read as a land where nods, signs of approval, are found

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a jocular name for sleep, read literally as a country full of approving nods.

clue.text: Second town in Staffordshire rated prosperous

parts.note: Leek is a market town in Staffordshire, an English county

explanation.surface: A second Staffordshire town has been judged well off.
explanation.definitionFit: Sleek describes a well-fed, prosperous-looking appearance, so one rated thus seems affluent.

clue.text: Share some land

definitions.meaning: a portion allotted to someone is their share
a small plot of rented land for growing vegetables

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both an allocated portion and a rented vegetable plot in Britain.

clue.text: Washington singer discovered in a hostelry

annotationWithheld.why: Washington singer discovered in a hostelry (5): DINAH is hidden across discovereD IN A Hostelry, so 'discovered' and 'in' are both indicator and fodder; no other parse
annotationWithheld.clue: Washington singer discovered in a hostelry

clue.text: Puts up once more when his heartless anger erupts

indicators.note: the letters burst out into a new order
the middle letter of his is removed

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone has to redo the hanging after his temper explodes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' removes the I from HIS, leaving HS to be mixed with ANGER.
explanation.definitionFit: To hang pictures or curtains again is to put them up a second time.

clue.text: Administration for under ten pence is preposterous

indicators.note: something absurd or topsy-turvy, so the letters are thrown out of order

explanation.surface: Someone protests that charging under ten pence for management is absurd.
explanation.definitionFit: Superintendence is the act of overseeing and managing, i.e. administration.

clue.text: Want seaman to talk about judgment

parts.note: AB, able-bodied seaman, is a sailor

indicators.note: the word for judgment is to be spoken, giving its sound

parts.note: good sense is sound judgment

explanation.surface: A sailor wishes to discuss a ruling.
explanation.definitionFit: Want in the sense of lack: an absence of something is a want of it.

clue.text: For starters, never get huffy in game that turns with easy delivery

indicators.note: those opening letters are placed inside the game
the game name is turned round, read backwards

parts.note: pool is a cue game played on a table

indicators.note: the opening letters of the next three words are taken

explanation.surface: Advice to a sportsman: don't sulk in a game that keeps changing, it's an easy one.
explanation.walkthrough: POOL turned gives LOOP, and N, G, H go between its two Os.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket a long hop is a short-pitched ball that bounces high and is easy to hit.

clue.text: Parts of trunk road lead to city

indicators.note: only some letters of each word, their beginnings, are kept

explanation.surface: Sections of a main highway take you into the city.
explanation.walkthrough: The first three letters of 'trunk' and two of 'road' are kept. TRURO is the city of Cornwall, reached by the A30 trunk road.
explanation.definitionFit: Truro is Cornwall's only city, its cathedral city in the far south-west of England.

clue.text: He had a point to make in World War 1

definitions.text: He had a point to make in World War 1

parts.words: He had a point to make in World War 1
parts.note: the famous recruiting poster shows Lord ... pointing his finger at the viewer

explanation.definitionFit: Lord Kitchener, British war minister, is the face on the pointing 'Your country needs you' poster.

clue.text: The law allowing international to join Arsenal

indicators.note: the arsenal lets the abbreviation in, taking it inside

parts.note: ordnance is military stores and weapons, an arsenal

explanation.surface: A rule permits a foreign international player to sign for Arsenal football club.
explanation.walkthrough: Arsenal is the London football club in the surface, but here means weaponry.
explanation.definitionFit: An ordinance is an authoritative decree or local regulation, a piece of law.

clue.text: Wink at songbird after opening time in French resort

indicators.note: the pieces are placed inside the resort

parts.note: Nice is a resort on the French Riviera
a tit is a small songbird

indicators.note: the first letter of after is taken

explanation.surface: A tourist on the Riviera winks at a bird singing at opening time.
explanation.definitionFit: To nictitate is to blink or wink, so to wink at something.

clue.text: Depression makes graduate misbehave

parts.note: a BA is a Bachelor of Arts graduate
to sin is to do wrong

explanation.surface: A graduate's bad behaviour leads to depression.
explanation.definitionFit: A basin is a hollow or depression in the land.

clue.text: Nonsense, Flipper is champion passerine

parts.note: bull is slang for rubbish talk
a fin is a flipper

explanation.surface: Someone scoffs that the famous dolphin Flipper is a champion bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The bullfinch is a perching songbird, and perching birds are passerines.

clue.text: Blundered, having adjourned without defendant

indicators.note: the defendant abbreviation is taken away

parts.note: a postponed hearing is deferred
DEF is short for defendant

explanation.surface: The court made a mistake by adjourning in the absence of the accused.
explanation.definitionFit: To have erred is to have made a mistake, i.e. blundered.

clue.text: Moratorium on hatred

parts.note: re means on or concerning
spite is malice or hatred

explanation.surface: A suspension has been declared on hostility.
explanation.definitionFit: A respite is a temporary pause or delay, as a moratorium is.

clue.text: Got a clue — a devious one — for listing

indicators.note: twisty and indirect, so the letters wander from their order

explanation.surface: A setter boasts of finding a sly clue for a list.
explanation.definitionFit: A catalogue is a systematic list, the act of listing items.

clue.text: Sportsperson who'll do a turn on the floor

definitions.text: Sportsperson who'll do a turn on the floor

parts.words: Sportsperson who'll do a turn on the floor
parts.note: the floor exercise is an Olympic apparatus event, full of spins and twists, so the performer does turns there

explanation.definitionFit: Such athletes perform routines in the floor event, which includes spins and turns.

clue.text: Archivist sees Cornish pasties are off without specs!

indicators.note: the letters are disrupted into a new order, with some taken off

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A records keeper finds Cornish pasties gone bad, unable to read without glasses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without specs' removes S, P, E, C, S from CORNISH PASTIES; the remaining letters are rearranged. A Cornish pasty is a pastry filled with meat and vegetables.
explanation.definitionFit: A historian studies and records the past, like an archivist keeping records.

clue.text: Overcome being dismissed at work

parts.note: a batsman dismissed in cricket is out
to do is to work or perform

explanation.surface: Someone is overwhelmed at being sacked at work.
explanation.definitionFit: To outdo a rival is to surpass or overcome them.

clue.text: Knocks off coolers?

definitions.meaning: to knock off something is slang for stealing it
the cooler is slang for prison, as is the nick

explanation.definitionFit: Nick means steal, and a nick is a police station or jail, as is a cooler.

clue.text: Celebrated musical note

parts.note: Fame is a stage musical based on the film about a performing arts school
D is a musical note

explanation.surface: A much-praised note in music.
explanation.definitionFit: Famed means well known and renowned, i.e. celebrated.

clue.text: Bird leaves girl, who takes instead a little air

indicators.note: the bird departs from the girl's name
the girl's name receives a replacement in place of the bird

parts.note: Henrietta is a girl's name
a hen is a bird

explanation.surface: A bird flies off from a girl, who takes a small tune instead.
explanation.definitionFit: An arietta is a short aria, and an aria is an air, so a little air.

clue.text: Master to resume shortly, on the main road north

parts.note: cont is the short form of continue, to resume
the A1 is Britain's main north-south road, with 1 read as I

explanation.surface: A head teacher will carry on briefly, travelling up the A1.
explanation.walkthrough: The A1 is the longest numbered road in Britain, running from London to Edinburgh.
explanation.definitionFit: To contain one's feelings is to master or control them.

clue.text: What hope betters that of becoming the authority?

indicators.note: the letters turn into something else

explanation.surface: Someone wonders what chance improves the ruling body.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom for those in authority, the establishment in control.
